plan: [ This is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. With independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Underbidding risks losing when profitable; overbidding risks winning at a price above value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. Since there is only 1 round, no learning advantage exists. To maximize expected profit, set the sealed bid equal to my value so I stay in until the price reaches $31 and win precisely when it’s profitable. ]

[ This mechanism pays the second-highest sealed bid and awards to the highest sealed bid, equivalent to a Vickrey (second-price) auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true private value: overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest exceeds your value; underbidding forfeits positive surplus when you could have won cheaply. There’s no useful history (round 1 of 1), and values are independent. To maximize long-run/expected profit, bid truthfully. With value $6, set exit at 6. ]

[ With value 0, any positive bid risks winning at a positive price and yielding negative profit. In a second-price ascending auction, the dominant strategy is to bid one’s true value. There is only 1 round and no learning benefit. Therefore, bid 0 to guarantee no loss and maximize expected profit (0) given the value. If others bid positive, we lose and pay nothing; if tied at 0, outcome is random but price is 0. ]
